title: Kubernetes Storage and Workload Controllers: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on Kubernetes Volumes, PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims and StorageClasses, plus the StatefulSet, DaemonSet and Job controllers. It covers the mental model, workflow, kubectl usage, common mistakes and a closing cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Volumes, PersistentVolumes and Claims
points: A Pod volume outlives container restarts but not the Pod: emptyDir dies with the Pod, and hostPath mounts a node path and should be avoided in production

A PersistentVolume (PV) is a cluster-scoped storage resource; a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a namespaced request for storage. A PVC binds 1:1 to a PV that matches its size, accessModes and storageClassName

Access modes: ReadWriteOnce (RWO) mounts read-write on one node, ReadOnlyMany (ROX) is read-only on many nodes, ReadWriteMany (RWX) is read-write on many nodes, ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP) is one Pod only
Example: a PVC requesting 1Gi with accessModes [ReadWriteOnce], used in a Pod via volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName plus a volumeMounts entry

Gotchas: a PVC stuck in Pending means no matching PV or StorageClass; reclaimPolicy Delete wipes the data when the PVC is deleted; with Retain the PV goes to Released and cannot rebind until its claimRef is cleared

chapters.title: StorageClasses and Dynamic Provisioning
points: A StorageClass names a provisioner and holds parameters, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode and allowVolumeExpansion

Dynamic provisioning: a PVC with storageClassName creates its PV automatically. The default class is marked with the annotation storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true", and storageClassName: "" turns dynamic provisioning off
volumeBindingMode: Immediate binds as soon as the PVC is created; WaitForFirstConsumer waits until a Pod is scheduled, which avoids zone mismatches for topology-bound disks

Static vs dynamic: static means an admin pre-creates PVs by hand; dynamic creates them on demand from the class. Expansion works by editing the PVC's requests.storage upward only, never down, and needs allowVolumeExpansion: true
Gotchas: dynamic PVs default to reclaimPolicy Delete; storageClassName cannot be changed on an existing PVC; if no default class exists and no class is named, the PVC stays Pending

chapters.title: StatefulSets: Stable Identity and Storage
points: A StatefulSet gives Pods stable names (name-0 to name-N-1) and stable DNS such as name-0.<service>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local, which needs a headless Service (clusterIP: None) set in spec.serviceName
Pods are created in order 0 to N-1 and terminated in reverse order; podManagementPolicy: Parallel drops the ordering
volumeClaimTemplates create one PVC per Pod (for example data-web-0), and the PVC reattaches to the same-named Pod after a reschedule
StatefulSet vs Deployment: Deployment Pods are interchangeable and share one claim; StatefulSet Pods are unique, each with its own volume, and fit databases and brokers

Gotchas: scaling down or deleting a StatefulSet keeps its PVCs, so you must clean them up manually or set persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy; rolling updates go from the highest ordinal down, and updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition holds back lower ordinals for canaries

chapters.title: DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs
points: A DaemonSet runs one Pod on every matching node, for log shippers, node monitors and CNI agents. New nodes get a Pod automatically, and nodeSelector limits which nodes qualify
A Job runs Pods to completion: completions sets the number of successes, parallelism the number running at once, and backoffLimit the retries (default 6). restartPolicy must be OnFailure or Never
A CronJob spawns Jobs on a cron schedule; concurrencyPolicy is Allow, Forbid or Replace, startingDeadlineSeconds limits late starts, and timeZone sets the zone
Controller choice: Deployment for stateless replicas, StatefulSet for stable identity and storage, DaemonSet for one Pod per node, Job for run-once work, CronJob for scheduled work

Gotchas: finished Jobs and their Pods stay until you set ttlSecondsAfterFinished; DaemonSet Pods skip tainted nodes such as the control plane unless you add tolerations; restartPolicy: Always is rejected for Jobs

chapters.title: Storage and Controllers Cheat Sheet
points: Inspect storage: kubectl get pv,pvc,sc, and kubectl describe pvc <name> to read the Events behind a Pending claim
Change retention: kubectl patch pv <name> -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}' before deleting a claim you may need back
StatefulSet ops: kubectl get sts, kubectl scale sts <name> --replicas=N, kubectl rollout status sts/<name>, then kubectl delete pvc -l app=<label> to remove leftover claims
Run one-offs: kubectl create job --image= -- ; trigger a CronJob now with kubectl create job --from=cronjob/; read output with kubectl logs job/
Quick map: access modes RWO, ROX, RWX, RWOP; binding modes Immediate and WaitForFirstConsumer; reclaim policies Delete and Retain; kubectl get ds shows per-node DaemonSet coverage
